extracted.intended_audience: North Carolina citizens, state agencies, attorneys, rulemaking coordinators, and parties to contested administrative cases
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of the North Carolina Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH) roles, divisions, and procedural rules that govern contested cases, rule publication/review, and civil rights investigations in North Carolina.

rubrics_metrics.name: County courthouse contested-case procedural control
rubrics_metrics.description: When contested cases are scheduled to be heard in county courthouses, the emergency crisis administrative orders and protocols issued by the Senior Resident Superior Court judge in that county control and supersede directives issued by the Chief Administrative Law Judge for Raleigh.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to any of North Carolina’s one hundred counties; links to the county emergency orders are provided (e.g., Guilford, Haywood, Onslow, Mecklenburg). The emergency orders can also be found on the North Carolina Administrative Office of the Courts website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules Division responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rules Division performs legal analysis and administrative and technical work in the review, compilation, and publication of the NC Register and the NC Administrative Code; and provides administrative support and legal counsel to the Rules Review Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functions include review/compilation/publication of rulemaking materials and direct support to the Rules Review Commission (RRC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules Review Commission statutory authority and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rules Review Commission is charged with reviewing and approving rules adopted by state agencies; its statutory authority is G.S. 143B-30.1 and following.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission’s substantive review procedures are set by the General Assembly and codified in the Administrative Procedure Act, Chapter 150B, Articles 1 and 2A; agency rules are reviewed/approved pursuant to these statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: OAH mission standards
rubrics_metrics.description: OAH must serve citizens with quality and efficiency by providing an independent forum for prompt and impartial resolution of administrative law contested cases; function as the State’s codifier, publisher, and reviewer of all administrative rules; and investigate alleged unlawful discrimination in employment and housing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statement frames organizational expectations: promptness, impartiality, quality, efficiency, and duties relating to rule codification/publication/review and civil rights investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil Rights Division scope of investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Civil Rights Division is a forum for investigating allegations of employment and housing discrimination based on race, color, sex, religion, national origin, age, disability, retaliation, physical or mental handicaps, or family status, filed by citizens of North Carolina.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the protected categories and the Division’s jurisdiction to investigate employment and housing discrimination complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearings Division role in contested cases
rubrics_metrics.description: The Hearings Division provides a forum for an independent hearing before an administrative law judge when a dispute with a state agency involving a person's rights, duties or privileges cannot be resolved through informal procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that formal ALJ hearings are the mechanism when informal resolution fails; implies procedural path from informal to formal adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: NC Register content purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The NC Register provides information relating to agency rulemaking, executive orders, contested case decisions and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the NC Register to locate notices of rulemaking, executive orders, and published contested-case decisions relevant to administrative law matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: NC Administrative Code publication/searchability
rubrics_metrics.description: The NC Administrative Code is published and searchable by title, chapter or keyword.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Code is the published compilation of agency rules; users should search by title/chapter/keyword to find applicable rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic review and expiration of existing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing rules are subject to periodic review and potential expiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site lists 'Periodic Review and Expiration of Existing Rules' as a topic — indicating a statutory/administrative process exists for regular review and potential expiration of rules, though specifics require following the linked materials or statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory foundation references
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevant statutory authorities for OAH and administrative procedure are cited (e.g., NCGS 150B Administrative Procedure Act; NCGS § 7A Establishment of OAH).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulemaking, review, and OAH authority derive from these cited North Carolina General Statutes; practitioners should consult these statutes for the detailed legal standards and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of ALJ decisions and meeting agendas
rubrics_metrics.description: The site provides access to Administrative Law Judge (ALJ) decisions and to meetings and events such as Rules Review Commission agendas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These resources support transparency and public access to decisions and RRC proceedings; users should consult them for precedents and upcoming public meeting information.
